class.name: PhysicsMaterial
class.brief_description: Surface properties and optional Fields material properties for physics bodies.
class.description: The existing friction, roughness, bounce and absorbency properties retain their native physics-server behavior. Fields properties start unset. Call the corresponding [code]has_...()[/code] method to distinguish an unset value from an explicitly assigned zero, and [code]clear_...()[/code] to return to inheritance. Inspector checkboxes expose the same flags. Scalar getters return the dormant stored value while unset, not the effective project default. With Fields, unset properties inherit from the complete material at project setting [code]physics/3d/fields/default_material[/code], registered by the Fields addon with default path [code]res://addons/fields/materials/presets/steel.tres[/code]. A body without an override uses that same default. The addon freezes one complete snapshot at Scene initialization, before project scenes load; edits to the default resource or setting apply at restart, and resource edits warn once. An incomplete or contradictory default is refused with an error naming the setting; there is no hard-coded fallback material. Only yield supports a Curve today. Heat capacities, density, conductivity and emissivity are constants; resistivity is an affine temperature fit. Other Curves will be supported when the engine has the corresponding tables. Fields validates an assignment or changed resource before accepting its revision. On refusal, the node keeps the user's resource, while simulation retains its last accepted revision; [method PhysicsServer3D.body_get_material] reads the simulated material. Native servers that do not opt in ignore these additional properties.

members.member: If [code]true[/code], subtracts the bounciness from the colliding object's bounciness instead of adding it.

The body's bounciness. Values range from [code]0[/code] (no bounce) to [code]1[/code] (full bounciness). [b]Note:[/b] Even with [member bounce] set to [code]1.0[/code], some energy will be lost over time due to linear and angular damping. To have a physics body that preserves all its energy over time, set [member bounce] to [code]1.0[/code], the body's linear damp mode to [b]Replace[/b] (if applicable), its linear damp to [code]0.0[/code], its angular damp mode to [b]Replace[/b] (if applicable), and its angular damp to [code]0.0[/code].
Assigned density. Mechanical mass overrides do not change this thermal/electrical material density. Unit: kg/m³. Unset initially; use [method has_density] and [method clear_density].
Constant opaque grey-body hemispherical emissivity between [code]0[/code] and [code]1[/code]. Unit: dimensionless. Unset initially; use [method has_emissivity] and [method clear_emissivity].
The body's friction. Values range from [code]0[/code] (frictionless) to [code]1[/code] (maximum friction).
Latent heat. Zero gives a zero-width enthalpy plateau. Unit: J/kg. Unset initially; use [method has_latent_heat] and [method clear_latent_heat].
Constant liquid specific heat. Unit: J/(kg K). Unset initially; use [method has_liquid_specific_heat] and [method clear_liquid_specific_heat].
Read-only content revision, advanced before the changed signal, including nested yield Curve edits. It is not serialized and is not a physical quantity.
Absolute melting temperature, used with the heat capacities and latent heat to derive enthalpy. Unit: K. Unset initially; use [method has_melting_temperature] and [method clear_melting_temperature].
Electrical resistivity at 293.15 K. Unit: Ω m. Unset initially; use [method has_resistivity] and [method clear_resistivity].

Signed coefficient in resistivity(T) = resistivity * (1 + coefficient * (T - 293.15 K)). Unit: 1/K. Unset initially; use [method has_resistivity_temperature_coefficient] and [method clear_resistivity_temperature_coefficient].

If [code]true[/code], the physics engine will use the friction of the object marked as "rough" when two objects collide. If [code]false[/code], the physics engine will use the lowest friction of all colliding objects instead. If [code]true[/code] for both colliding objects, the physics engine will use the highest friction.
Constant solid specific heat. Unit: J/(kg K). Unset initially; use [method has_specific_heat] and [method clear_specific_heat].
Constant thermal conductivity. Unit: W/(m K). Unset initially; use [method has_thermal_conductivity] and [method clear_thermal_conductivity].

Yield factor against absolute Kelvin temperature. A null Curve means constant factor 1 when yield is enabled. Linear Curves are represented exactly up to 32 points; more than 32 linear points or any non-positive factor is refused. Nonlinear Curves are sampled adaptively up to 32 points, warning if relative deviation exceeds 0.5%. Use a Kelvin domain rather than Curve's default normalized domain. Enabled, stress and Curve share one set flag; unsetting any returns the entire yield group to the project default.
Whether the material has a yield law. False explicitly selects an elastic law. Enabled, stress and Curve share one set flag; unsetting any returns the entire yield group to the project default.
Positive reference yield stress in Pa. Enabled, stress and Curve share one set flag; unsetting any returns the entire yield group to the project default.
